text:
Noah (CEO): Thanks for coming. Opening this thread for quick leadership clarifications on mission, positioning, market signals, and how we should talk about competitors. Keep Qs short.

Tara (Product): Quick: when we say 'production-first developer experience', is that primarily SDKs + docs, or do we call out runtime guarantees externally?

Rafael (CTO): Both. SDKs/docs are the entry; runtime guarantees (SLA, rollback, routing) are the proof points we include in mid-funnel and enterprise materials.

Ethan (Sales): Sales ask: whats the single line we should use on discovery calls vs hyperscaler endpoints?

Noah (CEO): One-liner: "Redwood gives predictable, production-grade inference with controls that shrink unit costs in real workloads." Use that as a starting point.

Lina (Marketing): Can we publish a tiny public metric set (uptime + latency attainment) without technical caveats? Marketing wants clarity.

Noah (CEO): Public: uptime and % of requests meeting latency SLO. Add a short footnote about workload variance. Deeper metrics go to partner docs.

Jules (Eng): For Dedicated customers: do we promise same rollout features (canary + rollback) day-one of pilot? Pilot questions need a crisp yes/no.

Rafael (CTO): Yes for pilot: canary + rollback will be available. Private GA will follow after compatibility tests; expect small lag.

Ethan (Sales): Competitor talk: should we ever use direct vendor names in sales decks or keep it comparative (features/outcomes)?

Noah (CEO): Keep it outcomes-focused: predictable economics, ops controls, private deployment options. Avoid direct vendor callouts in external materials.

Tara (Product): Product needs a short parity statement: "What matches across Hosted/Dedicated/Private"  what bullets should we include?

Rafael (CTO): Include: same API surface, core runtime primitives (batching, KV cache), security primitives (auth/KMS). Console/advanced analytics may lag.

Lina (Marketing): Can we get a 2-paragraph press blurb + 2-line sales blurb from leadership? Sales needs it for outreach today.

Noah (CEO): I'll post a press blurb and a tight sales blurb in 3 hours. Tag @Tara to integrate parity bullets.

Jules (Eng): Request: can eng share a small table of typical batching impact for short/med/long seq so sales has numbers on calls? even ranges are fine.

Rafael (CTO): We'll provide ranges (e.g., 1.2x-2.0x short, 1.5x-3.0x medium, 1.2x-1.8x long) with a short caveat. Engineering will upload to the assets folder.

ops-bot: Reminder: maintenance tonight 23:45-00:15 UTC; rolling updates, no expected customer downtime.

Ethan (Sales): One last quick: pricing model messaging  committed vs usage  what's the concise line?

Noah (CEO): "We support both usage pricing for flexibility and committed capacity for predictable throughput and unit cost."
